notes: robar = to steal, to rob.

sentences.text: Hubo un robo en el banco.
sentences.translation: There was a robbery at the bank.
The police are investigating the theft.

sentences.text: Los robos han subido este año.
sentences.translation: Thefts have gone up this year.
I'm not going to allow it.

sentences.text: Mi madre no me permite salir.
sentences.translation: My mother doesn't let me go out.
I won't let you talk to me like that.

sentences.text: Los niños juegan en el parque.
sentences.translation: The children play in the park.

notes: Irregular past participle: roto. romper con alguien = to break up with someone.

sentences.translation: I don't want to break anything.

sentences.text: Me encantan las series de policías.

notes: Countable in Spanish: una evidencia = a piece of evidence. Also la prueba.

sentences.translation: I bought a bottle of wine.

sentences.text: Hay botellas vacías por todas partes.

notes: hace viento = it's windy.

sentences.translation: There are very strong winds today.

notes: estar al mando = to be in charge.

sentences.text: No toques los mandos del avión.
¿Dónde está el mando de la tele?

notes: apoyar = to support.

sentences.text: El plan tiene el apoyo de todos.
La bala le dio en el brazo.
sentences.translation: The bullet hit him in the arm.

notes: pegar un tiro = to shoot. tirar = to throw.

sentences.text: Se oyeron tiros en la calle.
sentences.translation: Shots were heard in the street.

sentences.text: En esa época yo vivía sola.
Es la mejor época del año.
sentences.translation: It's the best time of the year.

notes: In Spain also a long weekend.

sentences.translation: We have to cross the bridge.

notes: a distancia = from a distance, remotely.

sentences.translation: How far is it to the town?

notes: el deseo = the wish. More formal than querer.

sentences.translation: We wish you lots of luck.

sentences.text: Es todo lo que podría desear.
sentences.translation: It's all I could wish for.

notes: pelearse con = to fight with; la pelea = the fight.

sentences.translation: I don't want to fight with you.
We had a fight again yesterday.

sentences.text: No te pelees con tu hermano.

notes: echar de menos = to miss (someone); echar un vistazo = to take a look.

sentences.translation: They threw me out of the bar.
Put a little salt on it.

sentences.text: Echó la pelota por la ventana.
sentences.translation: He threw the ball out the window.

notes: descansar = to rest.

sentences.text: Hacemos un descanso de diez minutos.

notes: Feminine, but el área in the singular (stressed a-), like el agua.

sentences.text: Hay áreas para niños en el parque.
sentences.translation: There are areas for children in the park.

notes: estar orgulloso de = to be proud of. el orgullo = pride.

sentences.text: Estamos muy orgullosos de nuestro equipo.
sentences.translation: We're very proud of our team.

notes: dar un espectáculo = to make a scene.

sentences.translation: The show is about to start.

sentences.text: Me enseñó un truco de magia.
sentences.translation: He showed me a magic trick.

sentences.text: Es un asunto de seguridad nacional.
sentences.translation: It's a matter of national security.
It was on the national news.

sentences.text: Eres el centro de mi universo.
sentences.translation: You're the center of my universe.
You have something on your nose.

notes: me da vergüenza = I'm embarrassed, I'm too shy to.

sentences.text: Me da vergüenza hablar en público.
sentences.translation: I'm embarrassed to speak in public.

sentences.text: Hay un monstruo debajo de mi cama.
sentences.translation: There's a monster under my bed.

sentences.text: La princesa vive en un castillo.
sentences.translation: The princess lives in a castle.

sentences.text: A mi hija le gustan las princesas.

notes: Also el bus. In Mexico el camión, in Argentina el colectivo.

sentences.translation: What time does the bus come?

gloss: to look after, to take care of
notes: cuidar a/de alguien = to look after someone.

sentences.text: ¿Quién va a cuidar a los niños?
sentences.translation: Who's going to look after the kids?

sentences.text: Mi abuela me cuida por las tardes.
sentences.translation: My grandmother looks after me in the afternoons.
How long does an egg take to cook?

notes: dar un paseo = to go for a walk.

sentences.translation: It was a very nice walk.

sentences.text: Me gustan los paseos por el bosque.
sentences.translation: I like walks in the forest.

notes: un detalle can also be a kind gesture or small gift.

sentences.translation: I pay attention to every detail.

sentences.text: La belleza no lo es todo.

notes: Stress shifts in some forms: envío, envías.
el primer ministro = the prime minister.

sentences.text: El ministro dará una rueda de prensa.
sentences.translation: The minister will hold a press conference.
The minister didn't want to talk.

notes: Irregular: conduzco, conduje. In Latin America often manejar.

sentences.translation: He was driving when it happened.
Don't talk on the phone while driving.
You have to accept the truth.

notes: Also a noun: un borracho = a drunk.

sentences.translation: She came home drunk last night.

sentences.text: Tengo un contrato de un año.

notes: Days are not capitalised in Spanish. el viernes = on Friday.

sentences.text: Los viernes salgo con mis amigos.
sentences.translation: On Fridays I go out with my friends.
We live in a free society.

sentences.text: Es un peligro para la sociedad.

notes: cargar = to carry, to load; to charge (a phone).

sentences.translation: The truck is carrying a big load.

sentences.text: No quiero ser una carga para ti.
sentences.translation: I don't want to be a burden to you.
Heavy loads go at the bottom.

notes: Also a noun: el presente = the present. tener presente = to keep in mind.

sentences.text: Todas las personas presentes lo vieron.

notes: dedo del pie = toe.

sentences.text: No me señales con el dedo.
sentences.translation: Don't point your finger at me.

notes: en oferta = on sale.

sentences.translation: There are deals at the store.

notes: Spelling: protejo (j before o and a).

sentences.text: El casco te protege la cabeza.
Recibí una carta de mi madre.
sentences.translation: I got a letter from my mother.

sentences.text: Nunca ha recibido un regalo así.
sentences.translation: She's never received a gift like that.

sentences.text: Él recibió la noticia en casa.
sentences.translation: He got the news at home.

gloss: to thank; to be grateful for
notes: Irregular: agradezco. agradecer algo = to be grateful for something.

sentences.translation: You don't need to thank me for anything.

sentences.text: Te agradecería un poco de silencio.
sentences.translation: I'd appreciate a bit of quiet.
My father is grateful to you.

notes: robar algo a alguien = to steal something from someone.
estar enamorado de = to be in love with. enamorarse = to fall in love.

sentences.translation: They seem very much in love.

notes: las películas del oeste = westerns.

sentences.text: El sol se pone por el oeste.
sentences.translation: The sun sets in the west.

sentences.text: Vivo en el oeste de la ciudad.
sentences.translation: I live in the west of the city.
He has wounds on his hands.

notes: de inmediato = immediately, right away.
Also a noun: un/una profesional = a professional.
a oscuras = in the dark.

sentences.text: Voy al mercado a comprar fruta.
sentences.translation: I'm going to the market to buy fruit.
It's the best on the market.

notes: Also an insult: ¡cerdo! = pig!

sentences.text: Mi tío tiene cerdos en su granja.
sentences.translation: My uncle has pigs on his farm.

notes: el/la líder.
Serious as in bad or dangerous. A serious person is serio.
Also a juror, and a judging panel.

sentences.text: El jurado ha tomado una decisión.
sentences.translation: The jury has reached a decision.

sentences.text: Los jurados no pueden hablar del caso.
sentences.translation: Jurors can't talk about the case.

notes: acordarse de = to remember. o becomes ue: me acuerdo.

sentences.translation: I didn't remember to call you.

sentences.text: Ella no se acuerda de nada.

notes: Irregular: desaparezco.

sentences.translation: What have you been up to lately?
He threw a stone at me.
The house is made of stone.
There are rocks on the path.

notes: tener la intención de = to intend to.

sentences.translation: What are you planning to do?

notes: de buen/mal humor = in a good/bad mood.

sentences.text: Me encanta tu sentido del humor.
sentences.translation: I love your sense of humor.
I'm in a good mood today.
Why are you in a bad mood?

notes: pesar = to weigh.

sentences.translation: I can't carry so much weight.

notes: el asesinato = the murder; el asesino = the murderer.

sentences.translation: He was murdered in his home.
The woman was murdered last night.
They tried to murder the king.

notes: en directo = live (on TV or radio).
Also a noun: la central = the headquarters, the station.

sentences.translation: I live in the central area.

sentences.text: Es la idea central del libro.
sentences.translation: It's the central idea of the book.

sentences.text: Las oficinas centrales están en la capital.
sentences.translation: The head offices are in the capital.

notes: Used with estar: estoy contento.

sentences.translation: Are you happy with your job?

sentences.text: No veo nada en esta oscuridad.
sentences.translation: I can't see anything in this darkness.
He came out of the darkness.

notes: Stress: actúo, actúas.

sentences.text: Está actuando de forma muy rara.

notes: e becomes ie: comienzo. Same as empezar.

sentences.text: La clase comienza a las nueve.

notes: detective privado = private detective.

sentences.translation: She has a very sad look.
There were a lot of strange looks.

notes: ¿Qué demonios…? = What on earth…?

sentences.translation: That kid is a little devil.

sentences.text: Dicen que la casa tiene un demonio.
sentences.translation: They say the house has a demon.

notes: el/la fiscal. Also an adjective: fiscal (taxes).

sentences.text: El fiscal quiere hablar con usted.
sentences.translation: The prosecutor wants to talk to you.

sentences.text: Los fiscales están en la sala.
sentences.translation: The prosecutors are in the courtroom.

sentences.text: Hay un perro en el jardín.
sentences.translation: There's a dog in the yard.

sentences.text: Los jardines del palacio son preciosos.

notes: Es natural que… = It's only natural that…
Free as in no cost. Free as in not busy is libre.

sentences.translation: They gave it to me for free.

notes: o becomes ue: cuesta. Me cuesta… = I find it hard to…

sentences.translation: How much did the trip cost you?

notes: marcar = to mark; to dial.

sentences.text: Tienes una marca en el cuello.
sentences.translation: You have a mark on your neck.

notes: Also precious: una piedra preciosa.

sentences.text: No tengo acceso a ese archivo.
sentences.translation: I don't have access to that file.
Who has access to the office?
I did it out of necessity.
Every child has their own needs.

notes: Feminine: la dueña.

sentences.text: ¿Quién es el dueño de este perro?
La dueña del bar es mi tía.
sentences.translation: The owner of the bar is my aunt.

sentences.text: Los dueños no están en casa.

notes: Irregular: merezco. merece la pena = it's worth it.

sentences.translation: She deserves to know the truth.

notes: e becomes ie or i: miento, mintió. la mentira = the lie.

sentences.translation: I lied to you, I'm sorry.

notes: imaginarse = to imagine, to picture.

sentences.text: Imagina que estás en la playa.
No te imaginas lo que pasó.

notes: Masculine even though it ends in -a: el fantasma.

sentences.text: Parece que has visto un fantasma.
sentences.translation: You look like you've seen a ghost.

sentences.text: Mi hijo va vestido de fantasma.
sentences.translation: My son is dressed as a ghost.

notes: el pollo = chicken (food, young bird); la gallina = hen.

sentences.text: Compré dos pollos en el mercado.
sentences.translation: I bought two chickens at the market.
He was away for several days.
